Replay

Declarative visual and audio routes

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Routes that need event identity or history

Use effect routes to turn journal changes into visual or audio cues that retain the same event identity through correction. Effect_Route2(Event, Value, Rig) connects a typed event projection, bounded visual cue pool and typed scene binding. Audio_Route(Event) connects an event-to-sound projection, bounded voices and a consumption ledger. Both consume ordinary journal changes, preserving occurrence IDs through update, confirmation and cancellation. They remain outside World and never rerun gameplay to create presentation.

A visual binding supplies:

  • project(Event) -> (Entity_View(Value), include) for detached initial geometry and paint data. Prefer stable event-kind selection.
  • Optional animate(view, age, seconds) -> view for root fade/motion over time.
  • View_Binding(Effect_State(Value), Rig) to cache children at attachment and paint value, age, duration and confirmation. Detach releases any rig-owned resources.
Odin
route: scenegd.Effect_Route2(Event, Flash_Value, Flash_Rig)
ok := scenegd.effect_route_load(&route, parent, "res://flash.tscn", epoch,
    0.3, binding, capacity=32)
for change in changes { scenegd.effect_route_change(&route, change) }
error := scenegd.effect_route_frame(&route, render_delta)

Journal policy already determines speculative or watched delivery. Default route policy Journal follows it. Confirmed delays this route until a confirmed Begin or Confirm, useful for effects that should not be shown speculatively. The first accepted start creates a lifetime; Update changes its value, Confirm marks it, and Cancel retires it. Neither Update nor Confirm restarts its age or scene. Reused slots get fresh generations and child bindings. Expired, canceled and capacity- dropped IDs remain consumed so replay cannot restart them.

Changing the filter to exclude an active event cancels it. A later Update does not invent a speculative Begin; use a stable event category for routing, and ordinary value changes for animation. When a confirmed-only effect has not begun, its Confirm may start it, subject to its consumption ledger.

effect_route_clear removes live visuals without forgetting consumed IDs. effect_route_epoch requires a strictly newer epoch, clears visuals and resets the ledger/bindings. effect_route_retire advances the floor only when the caller knows no new Begin at or below it can arrive, including delayed watched/confirmed events. Do not use the render clock as that frontier. Full cue pools drop new effects; check route.route.cues.stats. Ledger history/per-tick capacity is explicit. Root properties and Rig lifetimes follow the view ownership contract. Scene instances are created on entry; bounded capacity does not mean prewarming.

For audio, the callback returns (Audio_Cue, include) and may borrow streams from a presentation asset owner through user. Godot players retain their own stream reference while assigned. Destroy the route before the parent or borrowed callback owner. Each route owns its own bounded voices and ID ledger:

Odin
audio: scenegd.Audio_Route(Event)
ok := scenegd.audio_route_init(&audio, parent, epoch, sound_for_event,
    &sound_bank, .Confirmed, world_voices=8, screen_voices=2)
for change in changes { scenegd.audio_route_change(&audio, change) }

Update moves an active spatial voice; it does not change the clip or restart playback. Confirmed-only routes play once upon confirmation. Cancel stops only a voice still owned by that occurrence, so canceling a stolen old voice cannot stop its replacement. Full voice pools steal in bounded round-robin order; consumed IDs remain tombstoned. audio_route_epoch clears voices under a newer epoch and audio_route_retire has the same safe-frontier requirement as visual routes. Use audio_pool_volume(&audio.pool, volume) for a local volume setting.

The pure view.Cue_Route(Event, Value) is also usable without Godot. Native and executed WASM corpus checks cover lifetime/overflow/epoch behavior. Actual Godot checks cover scene reuse, transform update, confirmation without restart, audio voice identity, cancellation, epoch rejection and resource cleanup. The scene fixture is compile-checked for WASM; it is not a browser audio-device claim.

Routes that need event identity or history#

audio_route_init_change accepts a callback with (user, Change(Event)), exposing the original occurrence ID/tick, change kind and confirmation state. It shares the same bounded voices, policy and consumption ledger as audio_route_init; choose one initializer. Cancel retires matching voices without calling either projector. A contextual projector sees the original Confirm even when the route delays its start until confirmation, so it can choose the correct historical placement.

Scrapyard uses this callback for pitch derived from the occurrence ID and wound positions reconstructed at the event tick. Event-only routing remains available when a sound depends only on its gameplay payload.
